questions.q: What does BACKUP DATABASE ... TO URL let a DBA do, and for which kind of SQL Server deployment?
options: Back up on-prem or VM-hosted SQL Server directly to Azure Blob Storage instead of local disk, while the DBA still controls the schedule
Automatically enable Azure SQL Database's built-in backup mechanism
Restore any database without needing a credential of any kind
Replace transaction log backups entirely with a single full backup
questions.explain: Backup to URL is a genuinely different third mechanism from both on-prem-to-disk backups and Azure SQL Database's fully automatic backups — it's for on-prem/VM SQL Server specifically.

questions.q: What one-time setup step does BACKUP ... TO URL require that BACKUP ... TO DISK does not?
options: Creating a SQL Server CREDENTIAL holding a storage account key or SAS token so SQL Server can authenticate to Azure
Installing a separate edition of SQL Server
Disabling the transaction log entirely
Configuring a VPN gateway to the storage account
questions.explain: The CREATE CREDENTIAL statement is the one addition — everything else (DIFFERENTIAL, NORECOVERY, restore-chain order) works exactly as covered earlier in the chapter.

questions.q: What does recovery point objective (RPO) measure, and what directly determines it?
options: How much data loss, in time, is acceptable if disaster strikes — determined directly by how often backups (especially log backups) are taken
How long a server is allowed to be offline before restoring
The total storage space consumed by all backup files
The number of databases a single backup job can cover
questions.explain: RPO isn't a number a DBA simply declares — it's a direct consequence of backup frequency. Tighter log backup intervals produce a smaller RPO.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why is backup-to-URL described as a 'deliberate middle ground' among the chapter's three backup mechanisms?
options: It gives off-site, durable storage like Azure SQL Database's automatic backups, while letting the DBA keep control of the schedule (and therefore RPO) like on-prem backups
It costs exactly half as much as the other two options
It is only available for databases smaller than 10GB
It combines full, differential, and log backups into a single file automatically
questions.explain: On-prem-to-disk gives full control but no built-in durability; Azure SQL Database gives durability but a fixed RPO. Backup to URL combines durability with DBA-controlled scheduling.

questions.q: What does Chapter 14 pick up immediately after this lesson closes Chapter 13?
options: High Availability & Disaster Recovery, including RTO (recovery time objective) as RPO's counterpart
A full return to writing T-SQL queries with no administration content
Chapter 13 repeated with different screenshots
Migrating on-prem databases to Azure for the first time
questions.explain: Chapter 14 is 8 lessons matching the real exam's 20-25% HA/DR weighting, starting with RTO — how long an outage can last — as the counterpart to this chapter's RPO.
